text:
Alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's scheduler change I started seeing a few 99.9th latency spikes on the dedicated GPU pool. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.internal/r/0x7f9a (redacted). attaching a short nsys snippet too.

Maria: ok can you paste the trace range and the query?

Alex: trace focus is 00:12:08-00:12:22, lots of small batches queued. root cause looks like queue wait >> kernel compute for a subset of requests. here's the top CPU slice:
```
nsys stats --report timeline
GPU queue time: 1.2s total
GPU active compute: 0.45s
Kernel launch gaps: 300-800us between small launches
Matmul kernels: many tiny cuBLASLt launches (~2-4ms each)
Custom fused kernels: fewer but longer (~10-15ms)
```

Jon: hmm that ratio means batching window is probably too small now or the scheduler created more small-priority slots. did we change priority preemption?

Alex: yes — the change introduced per-request priority buckets and made the continuous batching window adaptive. default max_window_ms went from 30 -> 8 for low-priority to reduce tail for heavy flows.

Sasha: and that interacts with the KV cache how? are we seeing cache misses causing more matmul for cold decodes?

Alex: good point. the trace shows repeated KV cache misses for a subset of sessions — likely due to a sweep interval bump. evictions + smaller windows => tiny launches more frequently.

perf-bot: automated-profile-summary:
- trace_id: 0x7f9a
- top hotspot: launch overhead / CPU scheduling (45% of GPU-wait)
- significant: kernel selection flip to cuBLASLt for 1-8 token lengths
- suggestion: test increased batching window or merge small requests at CPU side

Maria: can we get a perfetto flame showing thread affinity? I suspect CPU scheduler starvation from our worker threads moving cores after the change.

Alex: attached a perfetto slice screenshot (linked in trace). quick manual diff: before-change we had contiguous kernel launches (low inter-launch latency). after-change we have interleaved short idle slices on the GPU and jittery host-side scheduling.

Luke: two quick repro ideas:
1) simulate 80% cache-hit stream vs 40% cache-hit and measure queue_time/compute_time distribution.
2) A/B the batching window: keep all other changes but force max_window_ms=30 for low-priority and compare p99/p999.

Jon: also try forcing kernel selection to the older custom matmul for small shapes (env var RK_FORCE_MATMUL=custom) — if tail drops, it's a kernel-selection regression.

Sasha: I ran a quick local with RK_FORCE_MATMUL=custom + max_window_ms=30 on a 4-GPU dedicated sim and saw p99 ~120ms -> 85ms. interestingly queue_time dropped by ~60%.

Alex: that's promising. we should check if cuBLASLt path gets chosen because of a different workspace size or because the new scheduler fragments the batch shapes at runtime. nvprof shows many tiny handle calls.

perf-bot: note: nvcc kernel selection logs: many fallbacks to cublasLtGemm for shapes < 128x128 after updated kernel-probe.

Maria: action items:
- Alex: collect a pair of traces (A: with RK_FORCE_MATMUL=custom, B: with default) for same traffic slice (use replay) — include perfetto and nsys. (due EOD)
- Jon: instrument scheduler to emit batching_metrics: window_ms, merged_count, preemptions per-second. (due tomorrow morning)
- Sasha: run the cache-hit simulation and send quantitative distro of kv_hit_ratio vs queue_time. (due EOD)

Jon: I'll also add CPU affinity pinning toggle to see if core migration is amplifying launch gaps.

Alex: one more: add a short experiment to bump KV sweep interval back to previous value (we suspect sweep freq increased evictions). small risk but can be run on a canary pool.

Maria: great. set up a canary with force-matmul + pinned affinity + window_ms=30 and run 5k reqs. if p999 reduces by >20% we revert scheduler tweak.

Sasha: noted. I'll start the sim now and post results in this thread.

Alex: thanks all — will upload traces here when done. cc @perf-bot for automated diff once both traces are in. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: will perform diff when both traces available and post kernel-level breakdown.

Luke: thanks team. short-term mitigation might be to raise default low-priority window to 20ms until we understand kernel selection flip.

Alex: agreed. starting trace collection now.
